title: Turn your photos into quick paintings with a built tool
summary: Simon Willison asked Claude Opus 5.5 High to build a web tool that paints any opened photo in seconds; the working result is live online.
agent_role: Claude wrote the whole browser tool from one prompt; Simon supplied the idea and published it.
outcome: Simon published the working tool, which paints photos like an oil painting.
what_they_did: Simon Willison gave Claude one prompt: build a page that opens a photo and quickly paints it with a simulated brush. Claude wrote the tool. It finds outlines in the image and needs no extra libraries.
how_it_went: Simon shared the finished tool online, along with a sample painting of a heron.
worth_knowing: He builds on an earlier experiment where Claude imitated a watercolor style, so trying different paint styles is an easy next step.
prompt: Build a small web page I can open in my browser. When I open a photo, it should paint a version of it in a few seconds on a drawing canvas, using simulated brush strokes in a [oil paint / watercolor / your chosen] style. Keep it to a single file with no outside libraries. Show me the finished page and explain how to adjust stroke size and speed.

curation.rationale: A small but working creative tool built from one shared prompt, with a live demo; thin on process and close to a single-turn build.
